title: Disorder-induced conducting edges on Kagomé lattice
authors: A. Chmeruk, D. Jones, L. Chioncel
abstract: Within a cluster extension of the coherent potential approximation, disorder averaging generates a non-local self-energy that renormalizes both diagonal and off-diagonal hopping terms of the non-interacting Kagome-lattice Hamiltonian. These renormalizations (of both nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hopping amplitudes) drive the system between two topologically trivial insulating states through an intermediate gapless phase characterized by conducting edge modes over a broad range of impurity concentrations. Our results demonstrate that multiple-scattering effects alone can generate emergent effective spin-orbit interactions and qualitatively modify the edge spectrum of disordered Kagome systems.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the effect of quenched disorder on the electronic structure of the Kagomé lattice using the cluster CPA. The key finding is that disorder-induced renormalization of hopping terms can drive the system into a gapless phase featuring conducting edge modes. This suggests that disorder can qualitatively modify the electronic spectrum in a manner reminiscent of topological phase transitions.
main_problem: The study investigates how disorder can induce conducting edge states on the Kagomé lattice, potentially mimicking or modifying topological behavior.
main_result: Disorder averaging generates a non-local self-energy that drives the system through a gapless phase characterized by conducting edge modes over a broad range of impurity concentrations.
method: The authors employ a cluster extension of the Coherent Potential Approximation (CPA) within a locator-interactor formalism to calculate disorder averages.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Kagomé lattice, analyzed in a strip geometry. The model starts with a non-interacting Hamiltonian including nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor couplings, and disorder is introduced via random on-site energies (binary mixture).
key_observables: Spectral function, Total Density of States (DOS), Partial Density of States (PDOS) for bulk and edge contributions, and the disorder self-energy ($\Sigma$).
important_parameters: Impurity concentration (disorder strength $\delta$), and the ratio of disorder effects versus intrinsic Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) strength.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the cluster CPA approximation, which treats fluctuations up to the cluster size, and the disorder is restricted to a binary mixture distribution.
figures_summary: Figures compare the spectral gap closure under disorder versus SOC. They show that the edge contribution to the PDOS is consistently larger than the bulk, and the spectral evolution due to disorder is qualitatively similar to SOC-driven changes.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the Hamiltonian and the CPA framework. It then calculates the spectral properties (DOS, PDOS) as a function of disorder strength, comparing these results to known SOC-driven topological transitions to analyze the origin of the gapless edge modes.
why_interesting: The work uses advanced many-body techniques (CPA) to study how quenched disorder can induce emergent, quasi-topological features (conducting edges) in a lattice model, which is highly relevant to understanding disorder effects in quantum materials.
